chunks: And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Does any of you come to his brother, put his hand in his pocket, take what he needs, and the other does not stop him?
I said: I do not know of that happening among us.
He said: So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Then (you have achieved) nothing.
He said: The community (of believers) have not attained maturity in their understanding yet.

key_terms.أَحْلَامُهُمْ: Their intellects/maturity (plural of حِلْم, meaning forbearance or sound judgment)
key_terms.فَلَا يَدْفَعُهُ: And he does not stop/prevent him

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam mean by the community not having received their 'ahlam' yet?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) uses this anecdote to critique the nascent Muslim community's lack of 'ahlam' (intellectual and social maturity), highlighting their passive tolerance of boundary violations. This reflects the early stage of communal development where the internalization of mutual rights had not yet fully matured into active enforcement.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 103. It has been reported that Abu Ja'far (a.s) asked:
Does any of you come to his brother, put his hand in his pocket and takes what he wants; and the other one does not stop him?'
I (the narrator) said, 'I do not know of that (happening) amongst us.'
So, Abu Ja'far (a.s) said, 'Then (you have achieved) nothing.'
I exclaimed. 'The community (of believers) have not attained maturity in their understanding yet,' he remarked.
